# Chapter 4 — Defender for Cloud Apps: Session Controls and Anomaly Detection by Organizational Segment

*Scoping Cloud Application Security to Organizational Position*

## Why Organizational Context Is Essential for MDCA

Defender for Cloud Apps monitors user behavior across cloud applications and produces anomaly detections when activity deviates from established baselines. The behavioral baseline is the critical variable. MDCA establishes baselines per user and per application, flagging deviations from the user's normal activity pattern. The limitation of this per-user baseline model is that it cannot differentiate between legitimate role-driven behavior and actual anomalies when the user's legitimate behavior is itself atypical relative to the broader tenant baseline.

A data analyst who downloads thousands of records from SharePoint and OneDrive daily as part of their normal workflow will trigger MDCA's bulk download detection if MDCA calibrates its threshold against the tenant-wide average download volume. The analyst is not a threat; the policy is miscalibrated for their organizational context. Conversely, a user in the legal department who downloads fifty documents in a session may fall well below the tenant-wide threshold that triggered the analyst's alert, but fifty documents from a legal matter library is a significant and potentially reportable event in that organizational context. Without organizational context, MDCA cannot differentiate these cases systematically. It either sets a global threshold that under-alerts for data-heavy roles or over-alerts for data-light roles — and neither outcome is operationally sustainable.

OrgPath resolves this by enabling per-segment session policy and anomaly detection configuration. MDCA's session controls are applied through Conditional Access App Control policies, which are Conditional Access policies with session control settings that route application traffic through MDCA's proxy for real-time inspection. When Conditional Access policies are scoped to OrgPath-derived dynamic user groups, the session control parameters — download limits, upload restrictions, file classification filters, session duration controls — are set per organizational segment rather than globally. The data analytics team receives a policy calibrated to their download volume norms. The legal department receives a policy calibrated to their much lower normal activity with correspondingly tighter anomaly thresholds.

## Conditional Access App Control Policy Creation by OrgPath Segment

The following PowerShell script creates a Conditional Access policy that applies MDCA session monitoring to a specific OrgPath user group. The script is parameterized so it can be called once per OrgPath node that requires a distinct MDCA session control policy. For nodes that share the same session control parameters, the parent branch group's policy provides coverage through dynamic group inheritance.

```powershell
#Requires -Modules Microsoft.Graph.Authentication, Microsoft.Graph.Beta.Identity.SignIns
<# data-id="215"
.SYNOPSIS
    Creates a Conditional Access policy applying MDCA session controls
    to a specific OrgPath branch user group.

.DESCRIPTION
    Creates a Conditional Access policy in report-only mode that routes
    sessions for users in the specified OrgPath branch group through
    Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps for real-time session monitoring.

    Start all policies in "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced" mode.
    Validate that no legitimate workflows are blocked by reviewing
    the sign-in log CA policy report in Entra ID for at least five
    business days before switching to "enabled".

.PARAMETER OrgBranchGroupId
    Entra ID group GUID of the ORG-BRANCH-{NodeId} user group for this segment.
    Retrieve with: (Get-MgGroup -Filter "displayName eq 'ORG-BRANCH-{NodeId}'").Id
    SUBSTITUTE: Replace with the actual GUID for each segment you are onboarding.

.PARAMETER NodeId
    OrgTree node ID for naming and tracking. Must match the node ID in the registry.
    Example: "FINANCE-ACCOUNTING"

.PARAMETER NodeName
    Human-readable name of the organizational segment. Used in the policy display name.
    Example: "Finance Accounting"

.PARAMETER CloudAppSecurityType
    MDCA session control type. Options:
      monitorOnly      — Monitor all session activity; no blocking
      blockDownloads   — Allow session but block all file downloads
      mcasConfigured   — Apply the app-specific MDCA policy configured in the MDCA portal
    SUBSTITUTE: Select appropriate control level per segment sensitivity.
    Start with monitorOnly for all segments during initial rollout.

.NOTES
    Required Graph scope: Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess
    Cloud app IDs are Entra ID service principal appIds for Microsoft cloud apps.
    20892 = SharePoint Online, 15600 = OneDrive for Business
    Add app IDs from the Entra ID Enterprise Applications blade for additional apps.
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]
    [string]$OrgBranchGroupId,

    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]
    [string]$NodeId,

    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]
    [string]$NodeName,

    [ValidateSet("monitorOnly","blockDownloads","mcasConfigured")]
    [string]$CloudAppSecurityType = "monitorOnly"
)

Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess" -NoWelcome

$policyBody = @{
    displayName = "MDCA Session Control — $NodeName (ORG-BRANCH-$NodeId)"

    # Start in report-only mode. Switch to "enabled" after validation.
    # SUBSTITUTE: Change to "enabled" after reviewing CA sign-in logs.
    state = "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"

    conditions = @{
        users = @{
            includeGroups = @($OrgBranchGroupId)
            # SUBSTITUTE: Add exclusion groups for break-glass and service accounts
            # that must not be routed through MDCA proxy.
            excludeGroups = @()
        }
        applications = @{
            # 20892 = SharePoint Online, 15600 = OneDrive for Business
            # SUBSTITUTE: Add additional Microsoft cloud app IDs as needed.
            # Find app IDs in Entra ID > Enterprise Applications > the app > Overview > Application ID.
            includeApplications = @("20892", "15600")
        }
        # Apply to all client types — browser and modern auth desktop/mobile clients.
        clientAppTypes = @("browser", "mobileAppsAndDesktopClients")

        # SUBSTITUTE: Add location conditions if the segment has defined work location policies.
        # locations = @{ includeLocations = @("AllTrusted"); excludeLocations = @() }
    }

    # No grant controls — this policy applies session controls only.
    # Access is governed by separate Conditional Access policies.
    grantControls = $null

    sessionControls = @{
        cloudAppSecurity = @{
            # cloudAppSecurityType controls what MDCA does with the routed session.
            # monitorOnly: Inspect and log; no enforcement actions.
            # blockDownloads: Block all file download attempts.
            # mcasConfigured: Apply the per-app MDCA portal policy for this app.
            cloudAppSecurityType = $CloudAppSecurityType
            isEnabled = $true
        }
        # Re-authentication every 4 hours for sessions under MDCA monitoring.
        # SUBSTITUTE: Adjust frequency per segment risk tolerance.
        signInFrequency = @{
            value             = 4
            type              = "hours"
            authenticationType = "primaryAndSecondaryAuthentication"
            frequencyInterval  = "timeBased"
            isEnabled          = $true
        }
    }
}

$result = Invoke-MgGraphRequest `
    -Method POST `
    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies" `
    -Body ($policyBody | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10) `
    -ContentType "application/json"

Write-Host "[SUCCESS] Created CA policy ID: $($result.id)"
Write-Host "          Display Name: MDCA Session Control — $NodeName"
Write-Host "          State: Report-only (validate before enforcing)"
Write-Host "          Segment: $NodeId | Group: $OrgBranchGroupId"

Disconnect-MgGraph
```

## MDCA Activity Anomaly Detection by OrgPath — Sentinel Workbook Query

The following KQL query is designed for use as a Sentinel workbook tile. It joins the MDCA activity stream from CloudAppEvents to the OrgPath lookup derived from the audit log, producing a per-segment summary of anomaly detections, bulk download events, and sensitive file accesses over the past twenty-four hours. This view gives the SOC an organizational map of cloud application risk that complements the identity risk view from the MDI queries in Chapter Three.

```kql
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// MDCA Activity Anomalies by OrgPath
// Table:   CloudAppEvents (populated when Defender XDR data connector
//          is enabled in Microsoft Sentinel)
// Purpose: Per-segment cloud app anomaly and sensitive access summary
// Use:     Sentinel workbook tile; set auto-refresh to 1 hour
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

// Build OrgPath lookup from Entra ID audit log.
// SUBSTITUTE: Match the exact displayName of your OrgPath extension attribute.
let UserOrgPaths = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(7d)
| where OperationName == "Update user"
| mv-expand Props = AdditionalDetails
| where tostring(Props.displayName) contains "OrgPath"
| extend
    UPN     = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName),
    OrgPath = tostring(Props.newValue)
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, OrgPath) by UPN
| project UPN, OrgPath;

CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(24h)
// Filter to events with a resolved account identity.
| where isnotempty(AccountId)
// AccountId in CloudAppEvents contains the UPN for Microsoft 365 apps.
// SUBSTITUTE: If your environment uses a different account identifier format,
// adjust the join key accordingly. For third-party apps, AccountId may be an email address.
| join kind=leftouter UserOrgPaths on $left.AccountId == $right.UPN
// Users with no OrgPath assignment are flagged as UNPOSITIONED.
// UNPOSITIONED activity should be investigated — these may be unmanaged accounts.
| extend OrgPath = iif(isempty(OrgPath), "UNPOSITIONED", OrgPath)
| summarize
    TotalEvents       = count(),
    // Anomaly events: those flagged by MDCA policy or behavioral detection.
    // ActionType contains "Anomaly" covers MDCA's built-in anomaly detections.
    // ActionType contains "Policy" covers custom MDCA policy violations.
    AnomalyEvents     = countif(ActionType contains "Anomaly" or ActionType contains "Policy"),
    // BulkDownloads: File download events — volume indicates potential data staging.
    BulkDownloadCount = countif(ActionType == "FileDownloaded"),
    // SensitiveAccess: Events involving files with sensitivity labels applied.
    // Sensitivity field is populated when Microsoft Purview labels are in scope.
    SensitiveAccess   = countif(Sensitivity contains "Confidential"
                              or Sensitivity contains "Restricted"
                              or Sensitivity contains "Highly Confidential"),
    UniqueUsers       = dcount(AccountId),
    UniqueApps        = dcount(Application)
    by OrgPath, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
// Focus the workbook tile on segments with detected anomalies or elevated sensitive access.
// SUBSTITUTE: Adjust thresholds to match your environment's normal sensitivity label volume.
| where AnomalyEvents > 0 or SensitiveAccess > 5
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    OrgPath,
    TotalEvents,
    AnomalyEvents,
    BulkDownloadCount,
    SensitiveAccess,
    UniqueUsers,
    UniqueApps
| order by AnomalyEvents desc, SensitiveAccess desc
```
